title: Bases of flat modules over a local ring with nilpotent maximal ideal
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a local ring whose maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ is nilpotent ($\mathfrak m^N=0$ for some $N$; e.g. an Artinian local ring), and let $M$ be a flat $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], not necessarily finitely generated. Let $A$ be a set and $(x_\alpha)_{\alpha\in A}$ a family of elements of $M$, with images $\overline x_\alpha\in M/\mathfrak mM$. Then the following are equivalent: (1) $(\overline x_\alpha)_{\alpha\in A}$ is a basis of the $R/\mathfrak m$-vector space $M/\mathfrak mM$; (2) $(x_\alpha)_{\alpha\in A}$ is a basis of $M$ as an $R$-module (the $R$-linear map $\bigoplus_{\alpha\in A}R\to M$, $e_\alpha\mapsto x_\alpha$, is an isomorphism).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 051F (lemma-local-artinian-basis-when-flat, line 24295); its proof uses Nakayama's Lemma Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK, nilpotent case) and Lemma Tag 00HL (lemma-flat-tor-zero, line 9037)

proof.text: (Notation.) Let $\kappa=R/\mathfrak m$, let $F=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in A}R$ with standard basis $(e_\alpha)$, and let $\varphi:F\to M$ be the $R$-linear map $e_\alpha\mapsto x_\alpha$. Reducing modulo $\mathfrak m$, $F/\mathfrak mF=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in A}\kappa$ (componentwise: $\mathfrak mF=\bigoplus_\alpha\mathfrak m$), with basis the classes $\bar e_\alpha$, and $\varphi$ induces the $\kappa$-linear map $\bar\varphi:F/\mathfrak mF\to M/\mathfrak mM$, $\bar e_\alpha\mapsto\overline x_\alpha$. Thus (1) says exactly that $\bar\varphi$ is bijective, and (2) says exactly that $\varphi$ is bijective.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 051F (lemma-local-artinian-basis-when-flat, lines 24308-24321)

proof.text: ((2) $\Rightarrow$ (1); Stacks: 'immediate'.) If $\varphi$ is an isomorphism, then $\varphi(\mathfrak mF)=\mathfrak m\varphi(F)=\mathfrak mM$, so $\varphi$ induces an isomorphism $F/\mathfrak mF\to M/\mathfrak mM$, which is $\bar\varphi$; by step 1 this is (1).

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 051F (lemma-local-artinian-basis-when-flat, lines 24308-24321)

proof.text: ((1) $\Rightarrow$ (2), surjectivity; Stacks: 'By Nakayama's Lemma the elements $x_\alpha$ generate $M$'.) Assume (1). Then $\bar\varphi:F/\mathfrak mF\to M/\mathfrak mM$ is surjective (step 1). Since $\mathfrak m$ is nilpotent, Nakayama's lemma for a nilpotent ideal [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-nilpotent], applied to $I=\mathfrak m$ and $u=\varphi:F\to M$ (no finiteness needed), gives that $\varphi$ is surjective, i.e. the $x_\alpha$ generate $M$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 051F (lemma-local-artinian-basis-when-flat, lines 24308-24321)

proof.text: (The short exact sequence and its reduction; Stacks: 'one gets a short exact sequence $0\to K\to\bigoplus_{\alpha}R\to M\to0$. Tensoring with $R/\mathfrak m$ and using Lemma 00HL'.) Let $K=\ker\varphi$ and $j:K\to F$ the inclusion; by step 3, $0\to K\xrightarrow{j}F\xrightarrow{\varphi}M\to0$ is a short exact sequence [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. Since $M$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective] with $N=\kappa$ gives that $0\to\kappa\otimes_RK\to\kappa\otimes_RF\to\kappa\otimes_RM\to0$ is exact.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 051F (lemma-local-artinian-basis-when-flat, lines 24308-24321)

proof.text: ($K/\mathfrak mK=0$; Stacks: 'we obtain $K/\mathfrak mK=0$', written out.) By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-over-quotient-ring] (1) with $J=\mathfrak m$, the maps $\kappa\otimes_RP\to P/\mathfrak mP$, $\bar r\otimes p\mapsto rp\bmod\mathfrak mP$, are isomorphisms for $P=K,F,M$; they are natural in $P$ (both sides are functorial and the formula commutes with $R$-linear maps), so the exact sequence of step 4 becomes the exact sequence $0\to K/\mathfrak mK\xrightarrow{\bar j}F/\mathfrak mF\xrightarrow{\bar\varphi}M/\mathfrak mM\to0$, where $\bar j,\bar\varphi$ are induced by $j,\varphi$. By (1) and step 1, $\bar\varphi$ is injective, so $\operatorname{im}\bar j=\ker\bar\varphi=0$; as $\bar j$ is injective, $K/\mathfrak mK=0$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 051F (lemma-local-artinian-basis-when-flat, lines 24308-24321)

proof.text: ($K=0$; Stacks: 'By Nakayama's Lemma we conclude $K=0$'.) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-nilpotent] with $I=\mathfrak m$ to the zero map $u:0\to K$: the induced map $0\to K/\mathfrak mK$ is surjective because $K/\mathfrak mK=0$ (step 5), hence $u$ is surjective, i.e. $K=0$ (this is the clause 'if $K=\mathfrak mK$ then $K=0$' of that node). So $\varphi$ is injective; with step 3 it is bijective, which is (2) by step 1.

lean.statement: theorem basis_iff_basisQuotient_of_nilpotent {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Flat R M] (hm : IsNilpotent (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)) {A : Type w} (x : A → M) : (∃ b : Basis A (R ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) (M ⧸ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R • (⊤ : Submodule R M))), ∀ a : A, b a = (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R • (⊤ : Submodule R M)).mkQ (x a)) ↔ (∃ b : Basis A R M, ∀ a : A, b a = x a)
